pr.title: feat: add user search endpoint with raw SQL queries
pr.author: dev-contributor

summary.assessment: This PR contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability and is missing adequate test coverage and service layer abstraction. Do not merge until these issues are resolved.

findings.title: SQL Injection via unsanitized user input
findings.description: The `q` query parameter is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string without parameterization. An attacker can craft a malicious URL to exfiltrate data, modify records, or drop tables.
findings.suggestion: Replace raw string interpolation with parameterized queries. Use `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', [req.query.q])` or switch to an ORM like Sequelize/Prisma that handles escaping automatically.

evidenceRefs.snippet:
const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%${req.query.q}%'`;
const result = await db.raw(query);
evidenceRefs.reason: Direct string interpolation of req.query.q into a SQL statement — textbook injection vector

agentResults.summary: Found 1 critical SQL injection vulnerability in the new user search endpoint. Raw user input is directly interpolated into a SQL query string without sanitization or parameterization.

findings.title: Direct database access in route handler violates service layer pattern
findings.description: The PR adds database calls directly in the Express route handler. The rest of the codebase uses a consistent service layer pattern (e.g., `UserService`, `AuthService`) to separate data access from request handling. This inconsistency creates maintenance debt and makes the code harder to test in isolation.
findings.suggestion: Extract database logic into `src/services/userService.js` and expose a `searchUsers(query)` method. The route handler should only call `UserService.searchUsers(req.query.q)` and return the result.

evidenceRefs.reason: Route handler directly imports and calls `db` — pattern not used anywhere else in src/routes/
Existing pattern that should be followed

agentResults.summary: The new route breaks the established service layer pattern used throughout the codebase, adding direct database access in a route handler. This creates inconsistency and regression risk.

findings.title: New search endpoint has no test coverage
findings.description: The PR introduces a new `GET /users/search` endpoint with non-trivial logic but adds no corresponding tests. The existing test suite in `test/routes/` has full coverage for all other endpoints. Edge cases like empty queries, special characters, and SQL metacharacters are completely untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a `test/routes/users.search.test.js` file covering: (1) basic search returning results, (2) empty query string, (3) no matching results (empty array), (4) special characters like `%`, `_`, `'`, and `--` that are SQL metacharacters.

evidenceRefs.reason: No test file for users search route exists in this directory

agentResults.summary: The new GET /users/search endpoint has zero test coverage. All other routes have corresponding test files. Missing tests for basic functionality, edge cases, and the SQL injection vectors identified by the security agent.
No public API documentation gaps detected. The new endpoint is internal and not part of the public API surface documented in README.md.
